entry.name: Timeline
entry.summary: Shows the real composition as separate front-to-back layer and group rows, with exact clip timing and expandable transform properties. Sequence tracks remain available for source editing and sound. Both views use the same project and programme clock.
entry.purpose: Displays clip occurrences, layers, audio cues and property keys on the shared programme clock.
available_to: signed-in users with owned project and applicable entitlement
workflow: Use a laptop or desktop with a screen at least 900 pixels wide and a precise pointer. Choose a tool in the left rail; its controls open in the inspector beside Preview. Scroll inside the inspector to reach its lower sections while keeping the preview and timeline visible.

Use Composition layers to inspect each title, artwork or scene on its own row. Expand a layer’s keyframes to edit its existing transform properties. Bars show clip timing; opacity, occlusion and parent group gates determine the picture.
Use At playhead to filter by current clip timing and all parent group gates. This display filter changes no project decisions. Use Sequence tracks for source footage and track mix controls.
Move an ordinary animated layer using its bar or arrow keys. Its canonical transform keys move by the same bounded delta. Undo restores layer timing and keys together.
Select a source, layer or group on its timeline row. Group bars remain available when property rows are collapsed.

Move a group with a pointer gesture or frame nudge; its descendant starts and keys move in one history transaction. Drag or nudge its In/Out edges to limit visibility while keeping child source edits and hidden keys.
Selecting a group focuses its property rows; select an ordinary child clip to edit that child’s keys. Graphics and child-track locks block group timing changes.

Use the normal source editing controls, undo/redo, save/reopen and export. Inspect the exact movie beside the editable timeline. Group splitting/duplication and source-occurrence attachment remain unsupported.

Download project backup saves the current editable project and available media. Select Include saved versions in backup when the saved-version history is also needed; this choice does not delete local versions. Owned media access is re-authorized when restoring.
entry.preview_behavior: Group In/Out uses a half-open programme-time visibility range around assembled child graphics. Group move shifts canonical child timing and keys, retaining source phase. The same derived group range clips linked motion cues for preview and export. Property focus and clip selection do not change the edit.
entry.render_behavior: The shared composition plan carries group timing into the CPU compositor. The existing inverse programme clock gates the group’s assembled output at the same In/Out range. Source clips, child animation and audio use their existing compilation paths.
limitations: This dated development snapshot does not establish professional or production readiness.

One real 20-second footage/title/music/SFX project exercises group pointer move, trim, opacity keys, locks, group deletion/undo, source split/history and exact cold reopen. Broader source-occurrence attachment/reordering, group split/duplicate, nested audio/video/owned 3D timing and continuous/full picture/sound remain unqualified. entry.name: Motion / Transform Keyframes
entry.summary: Edit property keys, spatial position handles and value/velocity graphs on the same editable project. Curve the route between paired positions while retaining ordinary history, saving and final compilation.
entry.purpose: Create deliberate editable movement and retain the same keys across manual editing, Director proposals, saving and final compilation.
available_to: signed-in users with owned project and applicable entitlement
workflow: Open Motion → Transform keyframes and choose the Target layer. Read X, Y, Scale, Rotate and Opacity at the playhead. Scroll down for keyframes, value/easing fields and the separate Start/End velocity and influence controls.
Show motion keyframes in the timeline and expand an ordinary visual layer or graphic group, including targets without animation keys.
Edit an unanimated property value and commit with Enter or blur; Escape cancels. Add the individual property key at the playhead to start animation.
Move the playhead and edit that animated property to write its next key. Inspect evaluated values and use previous/next keys, timeline nudges and the existing easing/curve inspector.
At each playhead position, inspect X, Y, Scale, Rotate, Opacity and Crop X/Y for the evaluated pose. A zero-opacity key displays 0% in Motion.

Drag empty property-lane space to box-select across expanded rows. Shift/Ctrl/Command adds; Alt subtracts; Escape or pointer cancellation restores the prior selection. Shift/Ctrl/Command-click also selects individual keys. Drag, frame-nudge, scale spacing, apply interpolation or delete with the batch toolbar.

Copy with the toolbar or Ctrl/Command+C. Choose Original layers or an existing visual layer in Paste to, then paste at the playhead with the toolbar or Ctrl/Command+V. A single-source-layer clipboard can target another layer; supported property values, spacing, easing and curves are retained with fresh key identities.

Owning-track locks prevent changes. Group values use their own five-property bounds; group key selection opens Composite with the shared curve editor. Undo/redo, save/reopen, render and inspect the current output. Static anchor geometry is not an animated property.

In Motion, Add position key writes an X/Y pair at the playhead. Drag a path point over the picture or nudge with Arrow keys (Shift increases the step). The picture follows the temporary drag; release commits the pair once, while Escape/cancellation restores the prior edit. Paths sample actual X/Y interpolation and map animated parent coordinates.

Select a timeline key, open Graph editor and choose Value graph or Velocity graph. Edit the interval arriving at that key. Signed velocity uses property units per programme second; endpoint influence preserves endpoint velocity. Numeric edits commit on Enter/blur and write the existing four cubic handles.
Once a transform is animated, Motion inspector value edits write a key at the playhead. The static fallback is retained for the base transform; it no longer overrides visible key-driven values.
Editing motion keys while viewing a completed movie switches After to Live Edit. The prior download remains available through Export; it is not presented as an updated movie.

For paired position keys, select the layer in Motion → Transform keyframes, place the playhead in the interval and choose Curve path. Drag or arrow-nudge the amber handles; release commits once and Escape cancels. Straighten path retains its endpoints. Check the changed route before export.
entry.preview_behavior: Evaluates canonical layer/group property keys on the existing preview clock. Keyed images take precedence over legacy CSS entrance animations and transitions. Nested groups apply evaluated parent transforms after child composition and clamp curve overshoot to the group control bounds. Broad raster, media, curves and continuous playback agreement remains unqualified.
entry.render_behavior: Uses the existing shared compiler/compositor and interpolation expressions where supported. Group keys retain canonical target ownership and are projected into the group composition plan; output time maps back to the programme clock. Inspect the actual exported movie; the status does not certify every combination.
limitations: This dated development snapshot does not establish professional or production readiness.

Two bounded masked image-effect edits preserve eight position/scale/rotation/opacity keys through native save/reopen/export. Inverted-polygon sampled picture passes; one ellipse raster pair still exceeds the strict colour bound. This does not qualify every mask/easing/media or legacy entrance clock.

One native nested image/two-motion project preserves 16 group keys across eight channels, including one custom X Bézier curve. Midpoint, property rows, nudge/lock, reset/remove/undo, save/cold reopen, CPU export and full timeline playback pass; four image geometry pairs pass and decoded source-tone audio is unchanged. Native retiming, broader curves, broader mask/blend combinations, video/owned 3D/deeper groups, full raster and live sound remain unqualified. Existing worker Bézier expressions approximate 32 samples; browser interpolation solves the curve.

Cross-layer paste requires a single source layer and a current-project destination supporting every copied property and value range. Missing targets, unsupported crop/group bounds, destination locks, half-frame timing collisions and programme overflow reject the whole paste. Original-layers mode supports mixed owners. Clipboard is local to this timeline component; it is not an OS/project interchange format. Freehand lasso and cross-project interchange are not qualified. Broad media/retiming/full picture and sound qualification remains open.

Velocity/influence edits write a custom cubic curve, including when converting an easing preset. Flat intervals cannot acquire movement through velocity alone. Influence is1–99%; speeds that exceed the supported handle range reject. Hold has a discontinuous step and no finite editable endpoint velocity. Worker custom curves retain the existing32-sample approximation.

Spatial handles are endpoint-relative position offsets, bounded to ±200 composition percent. The route uses paired neighboring X/Y keys; other keys retain their existing interpolation. Adding or retiming individual keys can change adjacent intervals. Automatic arc-length speed, roving keys, closed vector contours and vector-shape morphs are not provided by these handles.

Curved intervals share a sampled travel curve in preview and export. Travel progress stays on the authored route; it is distinct from constant screen-distance speed. Native proof covers one image and four intervals; broader retiming, animated parents, other media and whole picture/sound remain unqualified.

common_errors.resolution: Select an ordinary layer or a graphic group before adding its supported transform keys.
Unlock the applicable property/layer in the normal controls before editing.
Check current keys/source binding and the documented preview/final limitations; inspect mapped frames in the actual movie.

entry.name: Compositing
entry.summary: Combines ordinary layers and animated graphic groups with shared order, static masks, alpha-aware blending and editable group clip timing. Broad preview/export picture and sound agreement remains incomplete.
entry.purpose: Compose editable graphic hierarchies while preserving child-local edits, timing and property animation through the shared preview and render path.
available_to: signed-in users with owned project and applicable entitlement
workflow: Select an owned image or ordinary title in Studio Composite.
Enable its geometric mask and choose rectangle, ellipse or polygon.
For polygons, enter3–64 percentage points and commit with Enter/blur; invalid drafts are not applied and Escape cancels.
For rectangles, set Mask corner radius from0–50%;0 retains square mask corners.
Review feather/inversion and the actual export; whole alpha and broader stacks remain unqualified.
To transform graphics together, choose root layers/groups in Composite and use Group selected layers. Choose an existing root group with other roots to nest them.
Set group X/Y, scale, rotation and opacity; child edits and keys stay local. Use Composite arrows to reorder group roots or their children.

Add an individual group property key at the playhead, seek and edit its next value. Expand the group in the shared timeline for property values, key navigation and frame nudges; choose easing or a custom Bézier curve in Composite.

Enable the group mask and choose rectangle, ellipse or percentage polygon. Set rectangle corner radius, programme-unit feather and inversion. Polygon Enter/blur commits valid paths; Escape cancels invalid drafts. The group mask clips assembled children before its transform.

Choose a supported group blend mode to combine the assembled result with its sibling backdrop. Ordinary child blends stay inside the isolated parent group. Reset group mask clears only its mask; graphics locks prevent changes.

Reset transform removes that group’s keys and restores its neutral base. Remove group transform removes its keys and promotes children without baking. Undo/redo and save/reopen apply; inspect the exact final export.

Select the group clip bar to move all child clips and keys, or trim its In/Out visibility. Composite provides exact timing values, Fit to children and reversible Delete group and layers. Source and child-track locks protect the same operation.
entry.preview_behavior: Full-canvas nested wrappers evaluate existing canonical motion keys on the shared preview clock, preserve child edits and apply a shared SVG geometric mask before the group transform/opacity. CSS group isolation retains the sibling backdrop for group and child blending. One native Multiply/Screen nested image/two-motion edit with 16 group keys has four scoped geometry and image-interior color pairs; whole glyph/alpha/raster/picture/sound and broad modes/media remain unqualified.
entry.render_behavior: The shared compiler carries group mask/blend decisions and transform keys into the existing CPU compositor. The ordinary geometric matte rasterizer clips assembled local child alpha before transform/opacity; registered request-owned matte scratch is cleaned after the render. RGB blend color weights the blend result by backdrop alpha, preserving foreground color over transparent isolated parents. Group and child blending share the existing leaf compositor and inverse programme clock. Static/Normal paths retain previous pixels. Source/source-VFX/generated-caption stages remain separate; inspect the exact final movie.
limitations: Rectangle, ellipse and percentage-polygon image masks and crop animation have scoped native/export boundary evidence. This is deterministic geometry, not AI subject segmentation.

Group masks and blending are implemented as static decisions; path/radius/feather/inversion/blend animation, broader feather/inversion/modes/media, animated video-layer masks and full alpha/text/effect-order parity remain incomplete.
This dated development snapshot does not establish professional or production readiness.
Editable percentage-polygon paths and rectangle radius use the canonical mask object. This adds no animated path, neural segmentation, mask expansion or video-mask support.

The bounded inverted-polygon/shadow/glow/blur image stack passes four sampled colour pairs with transform/opacity keys. The ellipse stack retains a strict raster failure, and historical landscape edge failures remain open.

The layer stack has native image/title/two-motion history, cold reopen, exports and scoped visible-image occlusion evidence. Actual owned 3D cross-family export, whole motion/title raster, large/deeper stacks and full raster remain unqualified. Source footage/source VFX and generated captions retain their separate programme stages.

One native nested image/two-motion edit uses a feathered inner polygon/Multiply and outer rounded-rectangle/Screen while preserving all 16 group keys and child poses/keys. Controls/history/reset/lock/cold/export/full timeline playback and four geometry/image-interior RGB pairs pass; decoded source-tone audio is unchanged. All eight non-Normal modes pass actual FFmpeg transparent/partial/opaque-backdrop fixtures, not every native mode/media/stack. entry.summary: Builds a logo intro as ordinary editable artwork, masks, groups and motion keys. Image logos preserve their supplied gradient colours and lettering; vector components can move independently.
entry.purpose: Turn a supplied identity into an editable construction and readable brand resolve through the shared Studio controls.
available_to: signed-in users with owned project and applicable entitlement
supported_media: SVG logos with 1–8 top-level shapes or groups
workflow: Open Graphics → Logo motion in an owned programme at least eight seconds long.

Select a local image up to 250 KB or an SVG up to 100 KB, with a maximum of 4096 pixels per side. SVG files need a viewBox or numeric dimensions. Image logos use their visible alpha bounds as a viewport; the source file is not rewritten.
Choose the brand name, accent, background and an 8–14 second duration that fits the programme. Build editable logo motion at the programme start.

For an image with a left-hand symbol and separate lettering, enable Separate left symbol from wordmark. Symbol width places the search boundary; the builder follows transparent space and rejects cuts through opaque artwork. Three separately masked fragments assemble the symbol, which accelerates along forward routes before joining the original wordmark.

Enable Construct words from pieces to assemble the original bitmap wordmark from 2–16 interlocking slices. Five words each construct from three independently masked title pieces, with staggered rebounds before a continuous close.

Choose Piece choreography: Spring assembly keeps the symbol-first interlocking arrangement; Diamond cascade opens with four triangular pieces per word, moves each complete word into place, then assembles the original logo in centre-out diagonal slices.
Edit the resulting ordinary layers, masks, groups and keys. Undo removes the authored composition. Add and time sound through the normal Sound controls.
Review the actual preview, save/reopen and export through the existing Studio workflow.
entry.preview_behavior: The builder writes ordinary graphics into the existing project. SVG shapes become raster artwork. entry.summary: Author editable cubic artwork with single or compound contours, even-odd counters, fill/gradient and stroke; animate it with normal layer keys.
entry.purpose: Build editable graphic pieces without reducing their authoring geometry to a fixed bitmap.
available_to: signed-in users with owned project and applicable entitlement
supported_media: authored single-contour vector artwork on ordinary image layers
workflow: Open Graphics and expand Vector artwork · editable paths. Choose Add vector artwork.
Drag square points and round tangents; arrow keys nudge, Shift increases the step and Escape cancels a drag.
Split after point preserves the existing cubic route. Remove points or choose Corner point / Smooth point to reshape it.

Choose fill, gradient direction/colors and a visible stroke width/color. In Motion → Transform keyframes, select the artwork and animate Stroke start / Stroke end / Stroke offset, or use their timeline rows and value/velocity graph.
Save and reopen the project, then export and inspect the movie.
entry.preview_behavior: The safe SVG reflects contour decisions and evaluated stroke start/end/offset values in the ordinary image layer. Partial stroke length and offset use the same bounded 128-sample-per-cubic distance measure as export. The contour inspector retains the full editable route.
entry.render_behavior: The existing image compositor evaluates canonical stroke start/end/offset keys on the programme clock. It clips open paths or continuously joins wrapped closed-path intervals, preserves the fill, and applies normal layer transforms, masks/effects and composition. The cached image is not the geometry authority.
limitations: Version one retains a single 2–64-point contour. Version two provides one to eight contours with even-odd fill, up to 64 points each and 256 total. Percentage anchors and endpoint-relative tangents remain editable. No arbitrary SVG/PDF path importer or automatic bitmap/letter tracing; Logo Workshop uses exact pre-extracted bundled glyph contours.

Contour geometry, fill and stroke width/color remain static. Start/end are 0–100 percent of sampled path distance; start greater than or equal to end hides the outline while preserving fill. Offset is −1000 to 1000 percent: closed paths wrap continuously across their original seam, open paths clip at their endpoints. A full closed outline remains full under offset. No per-segment timing, contour morph keys, compound booleans or full pen/zoom workspace.

Native evidence is bounded to the retained artwork project. Whole raster/audio, arbitrary self-intersections, animated parents, broad retiming and professional/production creative qualification remain separate.

Version two adds one to eight contours, up to 64 nodes each and 256 total. Closed overlaps cut through the fill; stroke trim/offset follows each contour independently. Boolean unions/subtractions and morph keyframes remain separate.

Open Motion → Transform keyframes, select that title and edit Text progress. Reverse or hold its ordinary timeline keys and shape their value/velocity curves.

entry.name: Logo Workshop
entry.summary: Design a vector symbol and outlined brand lettering, edit their contours in Studio and download transparent SVG/PNG masters.
entry.purpose: Create reusable logo artwork and animate its individual pieces on the same Studio timeline.
available_to: signed-in users with owned project and applicable entitlement
supported_media: native vector artwork with bundled Inter 600/900 Latin letter outlines
workflow: Open Studio and choose Start a logo design to prepare a blank canvas through the ordinary owned-source flow. Open Creator Studio, then Graphics → Logo Workshop. Enter a name and choose Flow, Orbit or Facet.

In the Graphics inspector, the three symbol choices appear together. Enter the Brand name, choose Flow, Orbit or Facet, then use the Layout and Lettering fields below. Scroll down for spacing, symbol size, colours and the controls for adding or downloading the logo.
Choose horizontal, stacked or symbol-only layout, lettering weight, spacing, symbol size and colours. Optionally enable ordinary assembly motion keys.
Add logo to timeline. Select its symbol pieces or individual letter outlines under Vector artwork. Choose a contour to edit a counter or outer path.
Choose a logo group and colour, white or ink variant. Download an SVG or PNG transparent master from the current vector geometry and base layout.
Save/reopen or restore the native project; use normal Motion controls and the existing final export for a film.
entry.preview_behavior: The design draft and ordinary vector image layers use authored cubic contours and real even-odd counters. Accepted designs become normal grouped vector layers with ordinary motion keys.
entry.render_behavior: The shared compiler preserves compound vector geometry; the existing image compositor samples each contour and applies even-odd fill. Stroke trim/offset runs independently on each contour. Static masters use portable SVG paths and a transparent browser PNG, before timeline animation.
limitations: Three editable deterministic symbol families, not an unrestricted AI brief generator or automatic tracing of uploaded logos. Bundled A–Z/a–z letters, numbers, spaces, ampersand, period and hyphen; 1–32 characters, Inter 600/900.

Each outlined letter is a vector layer after creation. Change its contours or build a new wordmark from the name field; it is not a live text object and does not retain an editable text-to-outline binding.

Compound artwork supports one to eight contours, 2–64 points per contour (three if closed), at most 256 total. Overlapping fills use even-odd parity. This does not add boolean operations or contour morph animation.

Master downloads use a flat logo group, vector geometry and base transforms before motion. Masks, crops, rounded frames, glows, shadows and blends must be removed; nested or non-vector members are rejected. Whole film picture/audio, broader combinations, owner creative review and professional/production qualification remain separate.

Logo letter spacing supports signed drafts: Enter/blur commits; Escape or locking discards an uncommitted draft. The new blank entry prepares an eight-second canvas through the same upload, ownership and entitlement path as other Studio sources.
